name: Ithra
overview: Ithra is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Amasa, as recorded in 2 Samuel 17:25. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details in Scripture. His mention is brief and focused on his paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Ithra means 'abundance,' which may reflect a positive attribute or blessing. He is also referred to as Jether in 1 Kings 2:5, indicating a variant or alternate name, though no specific meaning is given for Jether in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ithra as the father of Amasa. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded or implied in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ithra’s significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his son Amasa, who appears in the historical accounts of Israel. Although Ithra himself is not a central figure, his mention establishes the lineage and background of Amasa, contributing to the broader historical and genealogical context of the biblical record.
